title: [finding] H14's "stale pm:blocking" verdict is repo-local while real dependents live cross-repo — following its prescribed remedy on #7917 would have severed a live objectui edge
body:
Found by the triage seat, 2026-08-20 ~08:1xZ round, while acting on the half-state patrol view (#9857). Filed for the skills lane's own triage (`.claude/` patrol tooling face). Not urgent — no state was damaged; the guidance was caught before being followed.

## The live instance

The 07:54Z sweep reports:

> **H14** #7917 — `pm:blocking` carried while NO open card's `Blocked-by:` line — body OR comment — targets it, judged against the full two-channel index — a stale derived cache. … Report-only: the remedy is the triage sweep's derivation pass dropping the label …

But #7917's dependent is **objectstack-ai/objectui#4356** — open, `pm:blocked`, its `Blocked-by: #7917` edge recorded on the objectui side (added 2026-08-19 when the #7917⇄ui#4356 cycle was converted to a chain). `check-half-states.mjs` sweeps **this repo only**, so its "full two-channel index" is complete over objectstack and structurally empty over the three sibling repos. The verdict is phrased as exhaustive ("judged against the full two-channel index") while the population it judged is not — and its prescribed remedy is precisely the action that would have broken the real edge: the triage derivation pass dropping `pm:blocking` from #7917, after which the selection order stops boosting the one card whose closure unblocks ui#4356.

This round kept the label and recorded the false positive here instead.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a caveat

- H14's row text actively instructs the deletion ("the remedy is the triage sweep's derivation pass dropping the label"). A repo-local index feeding a cross-repo state machine is the same gauge shape as #8941 (body-only grep vs comment-channel lines) one level up: the reader trusts the index's completeness claim, and the incompleteness is invisible in the row itself.
- Cross-repo `Blocked-by:` edges are protocol-legal and common (contract-first splits mandate them: `Blocked-by: <owner/repo>#<n>`), so this is not an exotic case.

## Directions (skills seat's call, not prescribed)

1. Cheapest: H14's row text stops claiming completeness and names the boundary ("no dependent found **in this repo**; cross-repo dependents are not swept — verify before dropping"), making the triage-side cross-check explicit duty.
2. Fuller: the patrol additionally greps the sibling repos' open blocked cards for `Blocked-by:` lines targeting this repo (the reverse of what the unlock scan already does), at whatever cost ceiling the patrol tolerates.
3. Middle: H14 skips cards whose own thread records a cross-repo dependent (e.g. a `Blocking:`/audit note left by the seat when the edge was created), turning the false positive into a documented suppression.

Refs: #9857 (the patrol view carrying the instance) · #8941 (the comment-channel gauge gap, same family) · #10102 (the backtick gauge gap, same family) · objectui#4356 (the live cross-repo dependent).
